name: Lancashire
description: Lancashire is a historic county in North West England with a strong industrial and textile heritage. Its landscape ranges from the Lancashire coast and urban towns such as Preston and Blackburn to the Forest of Bowland and rural valleys.

places.name: Pendle
places.description: A district in Lancashire named for Pendle Hill, infamous for the 1612 witch trials that made it one of England's most notorious folklore landmarks.

places.name: Blackburn with Darwen
places.description: A former cotton-milling powerhouse in Lancashire, its skyline still marked by Victorian mill chimneys. Home to Blackburn Cathedral and a strong regional football tradition at Ewood Park.

places.name: Blackpool
places.description: England's classic bucket-and-spade seaside resort, famous for its illuminations, the Blackpool Tower, and Pleasure Beach amusement park.

places.name: Burnley
places.description: A former cotton-mill town in Lancashire's Pennine foothills, its Victorian textile heritage still visible in the mill architecture. Home to Turf Moor, one of English football's oldest grounds.

places.name: Chorley
places.description: A market town in Lancashire known for its flat cakes, its Victorian covered market, and its proximity to the West Pennine Moors.

places.name: Fylde
places.description: A coastal district in Lancashire between Blackpool and the Ribble estuary, mostly flat farmland and small towns like Lytham St Annes, known for its genteel promenade.

places.name: Hyndburn
places.description: A former cotton-weaving town in Lancashire's Hyndburn valley, its mill heritage still visible in the local architecture.

places.name: Lancaster
places.description: A historic city in Lancashire on the River Lune, with a Norman castle that later served as a courthouse and prison, and deep ties to the 18th-century transatlantic trade.

places.name: Preston
places.description: A historic market and mill town in Lancashire, granted city status in 2002, with a guild history stretching back to 1179 and a still-celebrated 'Preston Guild' tradition.

places.name: Ribble Valley
places.description: A rural district in Lancashire around the market town of Clitheroe, known for its rolling countryside, the Forest of Bowland, and views of Pendle Hill, infamous for the 17th-century witch trials.

places.name: Rossendale
places.description: A district in Lancashire's Pennine valleys, its towns like Rawtenstall shaped by the cotton and footwear industries.

places.name: South Ribble
places.description: A district in Lancashire between Preston and the Ribble estuary, largely residential and suburban, with the historic village of Hoghton and its Tudor hall among its notable spots.

places.name: West Lancashire
places.description: A rural, flat agricultural district in Lancashire around the market town of Ormskirk, known for its bulb and vegetable farming.

places.name: Wyre
places.description: A coastal district in Lancashire including the resort town of Fleetwood and stretches of Fylde coast countryside, historically tied to the fishing industry.
